items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: I had a fellow named Benny Waters... And we went very well together.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah, that's existed for a long time.

Yeah, Chaque et Pische. But see, I was full every night. And I stayed there and took his business, and was getting them calls, and things. In fact, I didn't have to go to the Champs Elysees, sometimes it would be months before I'd go to the Champs Elysees, because too much was happening up at my kingdom. There was so much happening at Pigalle.
So I had a fellow named Benny Waters (PHONETIC). Now, he was a champ. Benny Waters is an old musician. Right now he'd be about 76, right now.

items.title: 68002_Benny Waters oral history interview
items.q: Jacques Butler had charge of the band, he hired me.

ctx.x: Then we had to get Gormand [?] , we had to get the other piano player, we had another one, a guy that he didn't want to go on the tour yet. So we had Guy, Guy didn't go either because - so we had to take a trombone player and play some gigs, you know, like that. But we did this tour and went all the way to Casablanca and down there, in the Canaries [?] , you know. Everybody came back and we - I still stay with Bill, see, I'm still with Bill, see, because we wrestled with that tour together - long tour, see,…
And this would be what, '56 or so?
